extracted.intended_audience: comedians, journalists, free-speech advocates, and general readers concerned with censorship and legal risks in India
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and cautionary principles for performing and publishing comedy in India amid legal and extra-legal pressures from Hindu nationalist groups and state authorities. Covers what kinds of content and conduct have triggered police action, prosecutions, and online harassment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid making derogatory remarks about Hindu gods/goddesses or religion
rubrics_metrics.description: Allegations that a comedian made ‘derogatory remarks on Hindu Gods n Goddesses’ were the basis for complaints and arrest (example: Munawar Faruqui arrested on allegations under Sections 295A and 269 of the IPC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if eyewitnesses say the joke was not made, complaints can lead to FIRs and arrest; material perceived as insulting religion can trigger police action, prolonged legal proceedings, and mob targeting. Treat jokes about religion as high-risk in the current political climate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid content that could be construed as intentionally wounding religious feelings
rubrics_metrics.description: Police complaints alleged acts such as ‘uttering words with the deliberate intent to wound religious feelings’ and conspiring with organisers to outrage religious feelings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broad statutory language can be used to press charges; comedians should be aware that ambiguity or perceived intent can be alleged by complainants. Clear framing, disclaimers, and sensitivity do not guarantee protection against prosecutions based on subjective claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comply with public-health rules when performing during a pandemic
rubrics_metrics.description: One FIR alleged negligence in performing during a pandemic in a manner likely to spread infectious disease (Section invoked in the Indore case).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organisers and performers should follow local COVID-19 guidelines and document compliance; failure to do so can be used as an additional criminal allegation even when the stated complaint is about content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid obscene props or actions in front of underage audience members
rubrics_metrics.description: Complaints included claims that another comedian showed ‘objectionable things like a condom’ in front of underage audience members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Material or props that could be characterized as obscene before minors can escalate complaints and legal exposure; be mindful of audience age and venue publicity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be cautious using obscene language or roast formats
rubrics_metrics.description: The AIB celebrity roast faced police complaints and mass outcry about the ‘obscene’ language used; videos were taken down and organisers faced threats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-profile formats that employ explicit language may lead to content removal, legal complaints, and personal safety threats. Consider platform rules, local decency norms, and possible legal ramifications before publishing/performing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise caution when making jokes about powerful political figures and the government
rubrics_metrics.description: Complaints were filed alleging jokes insulted the Minister of Home Affairs Amit Shah and other government actors; criticism of government has led to sedition and other charges in many cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Jokes targeting ruling-party figures can provoke both legal action and coordinated online/offline backlash from political supporters. Expect higher scrutiny and possibility of coordinated campaigns like hashtags, doxxing, and legal complaints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be aware that old content can resurface and provoke new backlash
rubrics_metrics.description: Several comedians apologised for jokes or videos made years earlier which were found and circulated again, resulting in threats and demands for apologies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain an awareness of one’s archive: decade-old performances can be dug up and used against performers. Consider content audits, takedowns where possible, and a plan for handling resurfaced material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect personal contact information and expect potential doxxing
rubrics_metrics.description: Comedians reported phone numbers and addresses leaked online after controversies, leading to threats and pressure on families.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit public disclosure of private/contact details, use professional channels, secure personal accounts, and have a response plan and legal counsel ready for doxxing incidents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid content that could be characterized as contempt of court or attacking judicial integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: The Supreme Court initiated contempt of court charges against comedian Kunal Kamra and illustrator Rachita Taneja for a meme and illustration implying protection of a TV editor by the court and government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Satire that suggests judicial bias or mocks court institutions can attract contempt proceedings; creators should weigh the legal risk of targeting the judiciary and consider legal advice before publishing such material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand the broad application of sedition and related laws to criticism
rubrics_metrics.description: A database found a sharp rise in sedition cases filed since 2014 for acts including personal communications on WhatsApp, emails, posters, slogans, and social media posts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Political criticism—online or offline—has been prosecuted under sedition and related statutes; comedians and organisers should be aware that common expressive acts can be framed as criminal, especially in states with aggressive enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know that apologies may not quell harassment and may have limited legal effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Many comedians issued public apologies for jokes, but apologising often did not stop doxxing, threats, or legal action (examples: Agrima Joshua, Aadar Malik, Rohan Joshi).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apologies can be a public-relations strategy but may not stop mob harassment or legal proceedings; plan crisis communications thoughtfully and coordinate with legal counsel and venue partners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-engagement with online abusers can be a strategic response
rubrics_metrics.description: Munawar Faruqui advised fans not to respond to abusive comments, saying ‘Internet arguments have no conclusion, no end.’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid escalating online conflicts; consider instructing fans not to engage, use moderation tools, and focus on de-escalation rather than public argumentation that can amplify attacks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize disproportionate risks faced by religious and caste minorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Muslim and other minority comedians reported heightened fear and risk; appearance or name can make artists more vulnerable to targeted action (‘If this kind of treatment can happen with Munawar, where does it leave the rest of us?’).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minority identity can increase legal and extra-legal vulnerability; minority performers should take additional precautions around safety, venue selection, and personal security planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare for protracted legal processes and secure legal support
rubrics_metrics.description: Accused performers and organisers faced repeated bail rejections and lengthy detentions; charges were sometimes vague and procedures contested in higher courts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Have access to legal counsel familiar with speech-related offences, understand bail risks, document events and compliance, and prepare for potentially long legal battles even if allegations are unsupported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use collective action and solidarity as protective and expressive tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Women comedians released a collaborative satirical video ‘Women Finally Apologise for Everything’ as a response to harassment; collective gestures have been used for visibility and critique.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Solidarity campaigns, collective statements, and coordinated artistic responses can raise awareness and offer mutual support, but also carry risk; plan such actions with safety and legal considerations in mind.
